unit.why: The division tells how the Maggid's disciples counter-excommunicated the Pinsk opponents and the Maggid foretold his own death. It then appends a separate printed tradition: at his burial the dead Maggid immersed himself in the mikveh.
unit.boundary_note: Division ends with a running-head/catchword fragment ('מחו' עשר מערכת ב׳ ... אורות') that belongs to the page furniture, not the story.

stories.summary_en: In 1772 the mitnagdim of Pinsk persecute R. Levi Yitzhak's household, and the Maggid's disciples, including R. Shneur Zalman, turn the bans back on the banners. The Maggid tells them that this cost them their head, his own life, but won the Hasidim the upper hand in every future dispute, and he dies that year on 19 Kislev.
